newsitem.title: USA: CBOT eyeing new class of wheat for world contract.
newsitem.headline: CBOT eyeing new class of wheat for world contract.

text.p: The Chicago Board of Trade is eyeing different classes of wheat for a proposed "world wheat contract," Patrick Arbor, chairman of the exchange said at a lunch meeting Monday.
"We're taking a look at better milling, better processing wheats," Arbor said.
The CBOT has long-term plans to launch an international wheat contract that could be more widely used as a hedge vehicle by other wheat growing nations and end-users.
Arbor said the soft red winter wheat now traded on the CBOT would be unsuitable for the new contract because of quality.

Although no specifics were offered, Arbor said the exchange was not seeking to take away business from the Kansas City Board of Trade where hard red winter wheat is traded or the Minneapolis Grain Exchange where spring wheat is traded.
Also at the meeting, Arbor reiterated the CBOT's strong opposition to the legalization of the trade of over-the-counter ag trade options.
"The CFTC is about to legalize ag trade options," Arbor said. "This could make hedge-to-arrives (cash contracts) look like child's play," Arbor said.

In its high-profile battle with the CFTC over proposed changes in the corn and soybean grain delivery system, Arbor again threatened legal action if a CBOT-sponsored plan was rejected by the regulatory agency.
Arbor said there was "no legal or economic" basis for rejection of the CBOT proposal.
The proposal submitted by the CBOT sets delivery points along the Illinois River and eliminates Toledo, Ohio and St. Louis, Mo., as delivery points.
A ruling on changes in the exchange's corn and soybean delivery is expected in July.
